I farm all 13.1 mu in the usual wheat-maize rotation because that fits my land, my water access, and the way my family works. Since some people in my household work off-farm, I will keep the plan steady and practical instead of doing anything complicated. For winter wheat, I will use improved seed, put most fertilizer up front with enough nitrogen to support tillering and grain filling, irrigate a few key times because I have well water, and do normal pest control only when needed. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize on the same land with hybrid seed because I care most about stable yield, keep fertilizer moderate but sufficient, irrigate fewer times because summer usually has more rain, and use rotary tillage to save labor and move quickly between crops. I will stay with the wheat-maize system I know well, because after 35 years of farming I trust a balanced, labor-saving plan more than a risky one.
